prompt: Here's our chat gateway's delivery code — a NestJS WebSocket gateway that fans out messages from Redis pub/sub to every socket joined to a room. Profiling shows the CPU spike in a "hot room" (a burst of messages landing within a few milliseconds of each other) isn't Redis at all — it's this `deliver()` method: every single incoming message triggers its own `server.to(roomId).emit(...)` call, so N messages back-to-back means N separate JSON encodes and N full walks over the room's socket list. Walk me through how you'd optimize this hot-room path without dropping a single message and without slowing down delivery to other, unrelated rooms.
